title: Disentangling intrinsic and extrinsic drivers of gill ectoparasitism in an endemic North African leuciscid
content:
Abstract

Seasonal variation in fish parasite burden reflects the interplay between parasite transmission, environmental conditions and host characteristics, yet the relative contributions of these factors remain incompletely understood in many wild freshwater fishes. We investigated gill ectoparasitism in the Maghrebian Bleak (Tropidophoxinellus callensis), a freshwater fish endemic to Algeria and Tunisia, examining variation in parasite burden in relation to season, host age, physiological condition and dietary breadth. Three ectoparasite taxa were identified, Gyrodactylus barbi, Trichodina sp. and Dactylogyrus fraternus, providing the first characterisation of the gill ectoparasite assemblage of this species. Parasite burden peaked in summer, and season remained significantly associated with ectoparasitism after accounting for host characteristics, although much of the explained variation was shared among predictors. Parasite abundance increased with host age in unadjusted analyses, but the relationship reversed after accounting for hepatic condition and other predictors. Furthermore, parasite burden exhibited a nonlinear relationship with hepatic condition, reaching its highest values at intermediate hepatosomatic indices. These findings demonstrate that seasonal variation in ectoparasitism is closely intertwined with host ontogeny and physiological condition, highlighting the importance of considering intrinsic and extrinsic factors jointly when investigating host–parasite relationships.
